topic_and_scope: A focused analysis of lipid biomarkers and their role in cardiometabolic disease risk, diagnosis, and therapy, drawing on five contributions that span mechanistic genetics, sex-specific lipid risk, ApoB utility, ApoB100 biology, and non-lipid drug effects, with attention to gaps and future directions.
main_themes: Expanded lipid biomarkers and mechanistic roles beyond traditional lipid panels
Personalized risk assessment incorporating sex and ethnicity
Measurement standardization, validation across populations, and integration into clinical practice
main_findings: ANGPTL8 R59W variant carriers show altered plasma metabolite profiles (acylcarnitines, phosphatidylcholines, cholesteryl esters, and α-aminoadipic acid) and increased inflammatory signaling, indicating broader metabolic influence beyond lipid regulation.

ApoB testing provides incremental risk stratification for cardiovascular disease in Korean adults, with up to 17.5% of participants showing isolated high ApoB without traditional lipid abnormalities, suggesting ApoB complements standard lipid panels.

key_gaps.description: Standardization and validation of novel lipid biomarkers (ApoB, small dense LDL, lipoprotein(a), omega-3 indices, ANGPTL, non-coding RNAs) across large, diverse populations are lacking.
Clear guidelines and robust sex- and ethnic-specific lipid thresholds and reference ranges are not yet established, hindering precise risk stratification across populations.

future_directions.title: Characterize functional impact of the ANGPTL8 R59W variant across diverse populations
future_directions.rationale: Conduct multi-omics and longitudinal cohort studies to delineate causal pathways linking ANGPTL8 R59W to inflammation and metabolic dysfunction in different ethnic groups. Use in vitro and in vivo models to map the downstream signaling networks and identify potential intervention points. This work will clarify whether ANGPTL8-targeted therapies could mitigate cardiometabolic risk and how effects may vary by ancestry.

future_directions.title: Develop and validate sex- and ethnicity-specific HDL-C reference ranges and risk thresholds
future_directions.rationale: The observed sex-specific nadirs and mortality associations for HDL-C suggest standard thresholds may misclassify risk. Large, diverse cohorts should be used to derive sex- and ethnicity-tailored HDL-C reference ranges and risk cutoffs. These thresholds should be integrated into risk calculators and validated against hard cardiovascular outcomes.

future_directions.title: Implement ApoB testing as a standard adjunct to lipid panels across diverse populations
future_directions.rationale: Isolated high ApoB without traditional lipid abnormalities was observed in a substantial subset of participants, indicating added predictive value beyond conventional panels. Prospective studies and cost-effectiveness analyses across multiple populations are needed to inform guideline updates and routine clinical adoption.

future_directions.title: Standardize assays and establish reference ranges for ApoB100 and other non-traditional biomarkers
future_directions.rationale: Variability in measurement methods hinders cross-study comparability and clinical decision-making. A coordinated effort to harmonize assays for ApoB100, Lp(a), small dense LDL, and related biomarkers with validated reference ranges will improve accuracy in risk stratification and enable meta-analytic synthesis.

future_directions.title: Elucidate ApoB100’s mechanistic role in atherogenesis and inflammation; explore targeting strategies
future_directions.rationale: ApoB100’s interactions with proteoglycans and involvement in inflammasome activation position it as a central driver of atherosclerosis. Detailed mechanistic studies and translational work should evaluate whether ApoB-targeted therapies can reduce plaque formation and inflammatory signaling, potentially benefiting patients with residual risk.

future_directions.title: Systematically evaluate pleiotropic effects of lipid-modifying therapies in diverse populations
future_directions.rationale: Therapies like statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors, bempedoic acid, ANGPTL3 inhibitors, and others have non-lipid effects on inflammation, vascular function, glucose metabolism, and possibly cancer pathways. Comparative effectiveness research across ethnic groups will identify subpopulations that gain broad benefits or face unique risks, informing personalized therapy choices.

future_directions.title: Develop integrated multi-biomarker risk models using machine learning for personalized cardiometabolic risk
future_directions.rationale: Combine ApoB, Lp(a), small dense LDL, omega-3 indices, ApoB100, ANGPTL markers, and non-coding RNAs with clinical data to build predictive models. Prospective validation in diverse cohorts is essential to assess incremental value over traditional risk scores and to create decision-support tools that guide testing and therapy adjustments in real-world settings.
